requirement:
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
rationale:
**Verdict: the requirement is met.** The implementation is fully marked `{impl}`, it is documented, and the tests cover the design space.

**Implementation, `src/outline/rust.rs`**
- `KINDS` (lines 118–142) maps these grammar nodes to outline kinds, all named by the `name` field:
  - `function_item` and `function_signature_item` become `fn`. This covers functions, methods and foreign or trait signatures.
  - `struct_item`, `enum_item`, `union_item`, `trait_item` and `mod_item` become `struct`, `enum`, `union`, `trait` and `mod`.
  - `const_item` and `static_item` become `const` and `static`.
  - `type_item` and `associated_type` become `type`.
  - `macro_definition` becomes `macro`.
- `impl_item` uses `impl_name` (lines 7–15). It names the node by the `type` field text, plus the `trait` field text when present. That gives `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]` from the syntactic text, with no type resolution.
- `foreign_mod_item` uses `extern_name` (lines 17–37). It names the node by the ABI string content, or `Rust` when there is no ABI. The requirement leaves extern naming open, so this fits.
- `use_declaration` is `NameRule::Anonymous`, as required.
- Item-position `macro_invocation` is also anonymous. `item_macro` and `in_item_list` (lines 39–53) restrict it to item position, so expression macros are not nodes. That fits "other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous".
- `extern_crate_declaration` becomes a named `extern-crate` node. It is an item, and the profile documents it.
- Each segment is built only from the segments of its syntactic ancestors in the same file. Nothing in the profile follows `mod x;` to another file, so modules are never resolved across files.
- Helper functions that implement other requirements (`is_comment`, `attaches`, the doc-comment helpers) carry their own `{impl}` markers. I found no unmarked behaviour that belongs to this requirement.

**Documentation:** `md/reference.md` (References and Outlines sections) documents the selector spelling:
- `kind[name]` and `kind@hash` segments, with `#N` for duplicates and percent-encoding of special characters.
- An impl's type and trait joined by a literal `/`.
- Anonymous `use` and item macros.
- Modules never resolved across files.
- A full Rust profile table.

**Tests**
- `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` covers:
  - nested modules, external `mod x;`, and nested fns;
  - inherent and trait impls, and an impl on an array type with encoded spaces and brackets;
  - trait items, including the associated type;
  - `extern "C"` and a bare `extern`, which gives `Rust`;
  - duplicate names, which become `#1` and `#2`;
  - macro definitions, unions, enums, consts, statics, type aliases and `extern crate`;
  - a round trip through `resolve` and the failure of ambiguous or missing selectors.
- `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` additionally checks that two `use` declarations get distinct anonymous `use@` selectors.
- `item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not` checks:
  - anonymous item macros at the top level, in an impl and in a module;
  - the generic impl name `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]`;
  - that expression macros inside function bodies produce no nodes.

These tests exercise every kind the requirement lists plus the naming and anonymity edge cases. I found no unacknowledged gaps.

text: :::{req} rust_item_selectors
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
:::{req} outlines
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline; other
nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline descendants appear under the
nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
